title: Prove the sharp uniform binary character remainder gap (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the sharp all-k remainder bound for the binary full-guard character sum of #4275, answering the structural-spectrum question in Ryanson Jonathan's #4607.

```text
one nonzero entry:        Z(c) = 7*3^(k-2)
at least two entries:     0 < Z(c) <= 19*3^(k-3), k >= 3
sharp example:            c_12 = c_13 = 1, all other entries zero
```

Claim type: scoped mathematical proof with an exhaustive finite local lemma. The new proof conditions on two or three vertices, allowing every induced unary field, and handles the remaining directed matchings by factorization. It needs no all-character k=6 table. The full probability inequality for arbitrary k remains open.

Package: `research/binary-character-remainder-gap/`. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit #4275 for the character law, #4599 for the four-event antecedent, Ryanson Jonathan #4607 for the five-event theorem and structural question, and the retained Cinna Davis/source527/commdata2338/Jose Manuel request and normalizer lineage. No predecessor executable or spectrum table is imported.

## Evidence

Before, the retained five-event package tabulated its fixed-size spectrum and left a uniform structural remainder bound open. The new reduction proves the sharp bound at every request count.

- Every local graph and unary field is enumerated: 4,080 configurations in total, including all 3,648 three-vertex configurations with at least two edges and all 16 reciprocal-pair fields.
- All 4,164 zero-diagonal characters at k=2,3,4 meet the bound and agree between literal three-state summation and the positive subset formula.
- Sharpness is checked at k=3..8. Invalid domains, a false bound of 18, and reciprocal-pair misclassification reject.
- Both registered warning-strict modes pass on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.15. Each direct registered command took 0.32 seconds locally. The committed-byte/source-history preflight passes for all five files.
- Official committed export/integrity check and isolated optimized Git-free replay pass. Final normal, optimized and exported receipts agree and bind all package-file hashes.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/binary-character-remainder-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/binary-character-remainder-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/binary-character-remainder-gap
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/binary-character-remainder-gap --check-source-history
```

Another machine may substitute its CPython 3.12 interpreter. Expected markers are `PASS_BINARY_CHARACTER_REMAINDER_GAP`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal result uses the written graph reduction and an exhaustive finite local lemma, without a formal-kernel check. Binary arithmetic, zero diagonal and the exact three-state weights are essential. Complete equality classification, all-k probability comparisons, general negative association, request production, header selection/emission and a complete paid physical caller remain open. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change is claimed. Lean, Docker and selected cold replay were not run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Combine the 19/21 remainder gap, negative single-entry multiplicity and exact finite-GL factor to obtain an explicit eventual product inequality for each fixed k. Its threshold and every smaller dimension remain separate obligations.
- Classify equality in the conditioned local lemma and outside-field triangle inequality to determine all third-mode character graphs.

## Related open work

No other open PR studying this full-guard character spectrum was found in the submission-time complete open-PR listing. Merged #4607 is the direct predecessor; merged #4275 and #4599 retain their separate formula and fixed-k probability claims. The completion refresh examined this account's eight other open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. They address different objects; none studies this full-guard character spectrum, so no new same-quantity comparison is required.
